attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No Yang-Mills estimate yet computes H and R from the reflected Wilson boundary OPE for mixed hairpin products.
steps: Normalize N_delta and B_delta by their diagonals; the same-theory target block is q_delta=Nhat_delta oslash Bhat_delta, so OS positivity is q_delta>=0 on each realized finite Wilson family.
Decompose C^n=C1 plus 1^perp. Since J vanishes on 1^perp, testing z in 1^perp gives z^*Hz>=0 as the first nonzero term.
Take the Schur complement against the positive J eigenline. It equals epsilon_delta PHP+epsilon_delta^2(PRP-(e^*HP)^*(e^*HP)/n)+o(epsilon_delta^2).
On K=ker(PHP), the first term vanishes; a negative second Schur form yields a negative eigenvalue for small collars.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The finite-dimensional perturbation lemma is valid, but the actual RG construction must still prove the quotient expansion and identify B_delta without changing the theory.

assumptions: N_delta is the closed-cone collar limit of regulated reflection-positive blocks; B_delta records only Wilson boundary OPE factors.
q_delta has a Hermitian two-term expansion for a fixed finite Wilson family, with epsilon_delta>0 and o(epsilon_delta^2) in operator norm.
Diagonal normalization removes harmless locked one-body congruences: q_{ii}=1+o(epsilon_delta^2).
The same finite family is realized in the gauge-invariant test algebra before and after cutoff removal.
definitions: source object: finite locked Wilson collar OS blocks N_delta and boundary anomaly blocks B_delta with positive diagonals, after cutoff removal in the RG topology.
target object: OS-positive same-theory continuum block M_delta=Nhat_delta oslash Bhat_delta and its boundary limit as collars collapse.
controlled interface: normalized Schur preimage q_delta=Nhat_delta oslash Bhat_delta; only finite reflected Wilson matrices are transported.
same-theory condition: Wilson-loop renormalization and test algebra are locked before the collar limit; no new boundary counterterm, quotient, or observable relabeling is allowed.

equations.label: normalized quotient expansion
equations.valid_when: valid when the reflected Wilson boundary OPE has a uniform two-term mixed-matrix expansion.

equations.label: first tangent positivity
equations.valid_when: valid for any q_delta positive semidefinite for arbitrarily small positive epsilon_delta.

equations.label: degenerate second Schur test
equations.valid_when: valid when K=ker(PHP|_{1^perp}); it is the second-order Schur complement after eliminating the J direction.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find z in 1^perp with z^*Hz<0, or z in K with z^*C_Kz<0; either gives a small-collar negative OS determinant.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Turns the Wilson boundary OPE into finite matrix obstructions beyond the first-order zero-sum test.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For finite locked Wilson collars with q_delta=Nhat_delta oslash Bhat_delta=J+epsilon_delta H+epsilon_delta^2 R+o(epsilon_delta^2), valid same-theory OS positivity forces PHP>=0 on 1^perp. If K=ker(PHP), it also forces the second Schur form C_K>=0. Either negative form is a falsifier.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if no uniform mixed Wilson quotient expansion can be made valid in the RG topology.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if H and the degenerate Schur form C_K are proved nonnegative for a dense locked Wilson core.
control_decision.reason: The branch now has a concrete finite-matrix perturbation test tied to computable Wilson boundary OPE coefficients.

dependency_updates.description: Adds first and second rank-one tangent tests for Wilson collar collapse after the closed-cone step.
dependency_updates.status: active; depends on boundary OPE coefficients

dependency_updates.description: The locked algebra must realize finite hairpin families rich enough to test H and C_K.
Needs convergence of normalized mixed Wilson quotient expansions, not only distributional Schwinger limits.

falsifiers: A boundary OPE calculation finds z in 1^perp with z^*Hz<0; this first-order falsifier breaks same-theory OS positivity.
PHP>=0 but some z in K has z^*C_Kz<0; pairwise first-order tests pass while a small-collar determinant becomes negative.
Mixed Wilson products lack an operator-norm two-term expansion, so the tangent bridge is not valid for the cutoff-removal topology.
B_delta has zero or oscillatory entries, or forces new Wilson renormalization at t=0; then q=N/B is not the same theory.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 216 learned that H>=0 on 1^perp is only the first gate. If H has null directions, the valid next obstruction is a Schur-complement second-order boundary OPE form. This gives a sharper falsifier than generic nonrank-one anomaly language.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute H and C_K for three reflected Wilson hairpins sharing one boundary footprint; test zero-sum and kernel vectors before invoking any log-CND semigroup.
